public_rationale: The evidence is consistent with continued human involvement, while also showing useful AI debugging assistance. Microsoft's experiment establishes limitations of its tested agent, not the future of debugging across the industry. The surveys measure reliance on humans and perceived usefulness, not autonomous displacement of debugging work. No decisive replacement event was found. Because “not about to” has no definite endpoint, the forecast remains unresolved under the open-horizon rule.
limitations: Survey responses about trust and usefulness are indirect measures of replacement.
One experimental agent does not establish the capabilities of all coding agents.
The 2026 evidence cannot by itself establish what happened in the immediate months after April 2025.

statement.excerpt: debugging is hard, and a big part of what coders do, and not about to be replaced.
statement.document_title: ”Those claiming we’re mere months away from AI agents replacing most programmers” should think again

from_speaker: a big part of what coders do
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that AI will not imminently take over human debugging work broadly across professional software development.
Replacement means independently completing most debugging work that humans would otherwise perform. Using AI to suggest fixes does not itself establish replacement.
The context points to months after April 2025, but supplies no definite last month. No numerical deadline is imposed.
The statements about difficulty and workload are supporting premises, not conditional antecedents that must occur before the forecast applies.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence that humans continued performing most debugging work throughout a clearly specified near-term period would support the forecast. Because the speaker supplied no definite endpoint, continued human involvement at isolated dates cannot conclusively settle it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated, representative evidence that AI agents independently took over most human debugging work across professional development within months of the post would contradict the forecast. Benchmark success or adoption for assistance alone would not suffice.

A conclusive supported outcome would require a justified deadline and comparable measurements covering that period; the post supplies no such deadline.
